title: Certified rational Tamagawa component groups
objective: Compute certified rational Tamagawa numbers for good, genus-2 almost-good, and supported semistable genus-2/3 reduction certificates using exact component lattices and Frobenius fixed classes
references: D. Dokchitser, V. Dokchitser, C. Maistret, A. Morgan, Arithmetic of hyperelliptic curves over local fields

oracles: Direct finite component-group enumeration with Frobenius on tiny weighted graphs

handoff.summary: Added a host-independent exact component-lattice engine, conversion of existing split rational cluster certificates in genus 2 and 3 via the DDMM Theorem D.18 length pairing, separate geometric and Frobenius-fixed rational invariant factors, recheckable certificates, atomic local/product APIs, and explicit unsupported statuses. Tiny lattices are checked by direct exhaustive class enumeration; current almost-good and split-cluster reduction records are exercised end to end.
risks: No curve-level Magma or Van Bommel Tamagawa fixture was available in this lane; every tamagawa-v1.json row is an independent finite-lattice enumeration oracle, and none should be represented as an external CAS oracle.

Existing ordinary-nodal local certificates omit node thicknesses, so they remain insufficient unless an explicit component pairing/Frobenius matrix is supplied; auto mode retries the richer split-cluster certificate when rational roots permit it.
Bad reduction at 2, wild/nonsemistable reduction, nonsplit cluster permutations not encoded by the current reduction record, and uncertified nonminimal models remain explicit unsupported states.
next_steps: Integrate HyperellipticCurve.tamagawa_number, local_tamagawa_data, and tamagawa_product through the shared model/public API lane.
Enrich ordinary-nodal and nonsplit cluster reduction certificates with exact metric thicknesses and Frobenius matrices, then feed those records to component_group_from_lattice.
Add versioned curve-level Magma and Van Bommel component-group fixtures when an oracle environment or corpus is available.
